lines.en: I shuffle sideways along the tide line.

lines.zh: 八条腿踩在沙上咔咔响。
lines.en: Eight legs click across the dry sand.
The sand is soft; I sink halfway in.
I march along holding both claws up.

lines.zh: 沙里埋着东西，我挖给你看。
lines.en: Something's buried in the sand. Watch me dig.
Do not step on me; my shell is thin.
I dig into sand, showing only my eyes.
The beach is hot; I hurry across it.
Three hearts; I walk carefully.
I go around the shell and keep crawling.
My claw tests the way; my legs follow.
I remember where the tide line lies.
Sand has worked into the seams of my shell.
I cross the whole beach sideways.

lines.zh: 我侧着身子挪，躲开那块尖石。
lines.en: I shift sideways around that sharp stone.
Wet sand walks easy. Dry sand slips.

lines.zh: 我顺着沙坡往下溜了一段。
lines.en: I slide a stretch down the sand slope.

lines.zh: 有人靠近海龟，我得赶过去。
lines.en: Someone's near a turtle. I need to get there.
I scrape at the sand and dig slowly.
Waves come and go; I stay put.
I fold my claws in against my chest.
A tiny crab watches me from a distance.
A gull's shadow sweeps over the sand.
My burrow is cooler than the open beach.
I lick the sand off my claw.
The tide sounds again and again, flat and steady.
I will wait for the light to fade.

lines.zh: 我把自己埋得只剩眼睛。
lines.en: I bury myself until only my eyes show.
I bury myself up to the eyes.
There are no other crabs on this beach.
My claws ache a little from digging.
I count the waves sliding back out.
Don't put your foot in my burrow.
What are you crouching down here for?
Do not grab me; I will pinch.
Your shoe is bigger than all of me.
Have you come to collect crab claws?
My eyes sit up on little stalks.
Only you and I are left on this beach.
I dig my burrow right beside your foot.
No net in your hands; good.
The wave comes; we both get wet.
My claw is numb from the blow.
My claw nearly got torn off.
I have only three hearts to spare.
I burrow into the sand to hide.
That blow made my shell ring.

lines.zh: 沙里的洞塌了，我卡住半身。
lines.en: My burrow caved and half of me is stuck.
It hurts enough to make me blow bubbles.
My blood is soaking into the sand.
My claws are buried in the sand.
I cannot even walk straight sideways.
Is that the smell of fish?
The thing you dropped is moving.
What's buried in the sand is mine.
Let me sniff it; I will not eat.
Rarely anything smells this good on the beach.
I edge sideways a little closer.
Do not pull your hand back; I cannot reach.
This smell makes me forget the tide.
I raise my claws and walk over slowly.
It smells like a good meal to me.
You kicked me right out of the sand.
The shell held, but now I am angry.
Move; you are taking up my sand.
My eight legs kick at empty water.
All eight legs kicked at the air.
Once upright, I will pinch you.
Your boot is blocking my burrow.
The sand is trampled into a mess.
I walk sideways around you.
Easy there; my shell is thin.
A mate arrives; I tap my claws.
We dig a little nest in the sand.
Her claws are bigger than mine.
Do not stare; this is serious business.
The tide will cover our burrow soon.
Two shadows side by side on the sand.
We tap our shells against each other.
Soon there will be tiny crabs in this sand.
She digs deeper; I keep watch outside.
The beach is quiet this season.
I pinch it and test its weight.
A dead fish? That is mine now.
I drag it back to my burrow to eat.
If my claw holds it, I keep it.
This thing is harder than a shell.
I carry it around, held high.
Do not take it; I pinched it first.
Too heavy; I can only drag it.
Whatever lies buried in the sand is mine.
I stuff it into the corner of my burrow.
That sea turtle is crawling too slowly.
Its flipper is right where my claw wants.
That turtle has taken over my sand.
I have fixed my eyes on its tail.
I am close, and it still does not know.
Its drag marks are still fresh in the sand.
It cannot right itself; perfect.
Even a hard shell has its soft spots.
I will drive it off this stretch of beach.
My claws are already raised high.
It heads for the water; I follow.
I scuttle sideways, throwing up sand.
The turtle's legs move faster than mine.
One step closer and I can pinch it.

lines.zh: 沙里的钳子已经张开了。
lines.en: The claws in the sand are open.
The incoming tide is helping it escape.
My claw snapped shut on empty sand.
The loose sand slows my running down.
It reaches the shallows; I stop.
This time it must not get away.
I caught its flipper in my claw!
It pulls into its shell; I am stuck.
My claws hit the shell; it is hard.

lines.zh: 我咬了一口皮革似的皮。
lines.en: I bite a mouthful of leathery skin.
It kicks its leg and flips me over.
With three hearts, I still pick this fight.
I clamp onto its tail and hold.
We roll together in the sand.
I won; this beach belongs to me.
My claw aches; I withdraw for now.
One more crab has joined this beach.
The hole I dug in the sand is mine.
It is busy along the tide line.
A companion digs ten steps away.
My shell is soft; I hide a while.
This whole stretch belongs to me alone.
A wave hits; I grip the wet sand.
The sun is out and the sand is warm.
First I find a stone to lean against.
Born here, I will guard this spot.
The sand burns like the bottom of a pan.
Dropped from a height; my shell hurts.
Water fills my shell; I cannot breathe.
The blast threw me up and back down.
Something has lodged in my shell.
This light numbs every joint I have.
Not even a dead fish on this beach.
Lightning hits the sand; I dig down.
The sand is gone; only emptiness remains.
